correctness.rationale: For \(q\ge4\) and \(d\ge3\), the coordinate-direction clique/square argument reconstructs every Hamming automorphism. Coordinate-status vectors thus classify marker pointwise-stabilizer orbits. Counting refinement recognizes each truncated distance vector after \(d-1\) rounds. One further round yields counts of all neighbor distance-displacements: unique two-block displacements identify both occupied block counts in each of three two-block partition types; unique singleton-to-singleton displacements identify three occupied counts in the discrete type; known n_pi totals give other statuses, and the first marker distance gives the remaining common-block status. Hence colors equal orbits by round d; stars and bars and multinomial counting give class totals and sizes. Code and recorded log replay 3,240 cases, including direct checks of every individual orbit size; finite samples are not an infinite proof. Boundary \(d=2\) cases are not claimed as original.

value.rationale: Arbitrary triple individualization is a canonical low-depth probe of highly symmetric finite graphs. The theorem gives full structural separation by a basic counting procedure for every dimension \(d\ge3\) and alphabet size \(q\ge4\), including the genuinely extra unmatched-symbol status of all-distinct-marker coordinates. It supplies a concrete upper refinement-depth bound, all five marker equality-pattern class-count factors and exact class sizes. These data refine the abstract Tinhofer criterion into a reproducible infinite-family classification and distinguish orbit complexity from equitable-partition ambiguity; it is not merely a single small-graph value.
